Articles

Using peabiru

Get started with peabiru
Travel-time matrices
Accessibility
Expanded and arrival matrices
Detailed itineraries

The legs of each trip, with their times, distances, routes and geometries: the fastest trip, the alternatives, and the street edges a trip uses.

Fares and Pareto frontiers

Fare structures, travel times within a budget, the trade-off between time and fare, and alternative itineraries with their fares.

Trip options

peabiru’s own trip planner: every trip worth considering between two points, on time, fare, transfers and walking, with the legs of each.

Facility location

Where to open new facilities (maximal covering, set covering, p-median, p-center) and supply against demand around each place (two-step floating catchment area), on the travel times of the network.

Elevation

Slope costs for walking and cycling from an elevation raster: the two cost functions, rasters in projected coordinate systems, voids, and results that do not depend on the machine.

Scenarios: car speeds and traffic stress

Change the car speed of streets, by way or by area, and the level of traffic stress cyclists meet, for one routing call.

Inspecting a network

Where points snap to the streets, the street and transit networks as sf, the dates with service, and the errors in the GTFS feeds.

Compared with r5r

What peabiru shares with r5r 2.5.0, how the results of the two are checked to be the same, every difference between them, and how to move a script from one to the other.

Examples

peabiru with sf and the tidyverse

From points to maps with the tools you already use: an sf grid, routing with the native pipe, dplyr on the tibbles peabiru returns, joins back to the geometry and ggplot2’s geom_sf().

Example: isochrones by mode

Areas reached from one point in Porto Alegre within 10, 20 and 30 minutes, walking, cycling, driving and by public transport.

Example: mapping access to jobs and schools

Travel times from one point to a grid, and the jobs and schools reachable within 30 minutes from every cell of Porto Alegre, walking and by public transport.

Example: how much a trip by public transport varies

Percentiles of the travel time on a frequency-based network, and one trip split into walking, waiting and riding, departure by departure.

Example: the Recife metropolitan region by public transport

The 14 municipalities of the Recife metropolitan region as one network, with the buses, the metro and the VLT of the GTFS feed of Grande Recife: isochrones by mode, access to schools and health units on a grid of the Censo 2022, what the rail lines add, how much a trip varies with the minute one leaves, and the options of one trip.

Example: access to schools and health care in Recife and Caruaru

From open data to accessibility for two cities of Pernambuco: an OpenStreetMap extract cut with osmium, the population of the Censo 2022 on a hexagonal grid, public schools from INEP and health units from CNES, and the walking, cycling and driving times to the nearest of each.

Example: terrain, in Pernambuco and in Salvador

What an elevation raster changes in walking and cycling times: the Recife metropolitan region as one network, six municipalities of Pernambuco from the coast to the Sertão, and Salvador, in Bahia, as the steepest case, with the Copernicus elevation model checked against the ground first: at 30 m it reads the roofs, and a flat district shows how much that costs.

Example: who reaches the jobs in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Belo Horizonte

Access to jobs, schools and health facilities by public transport in three Brazilian capitals with an official, open GTFS feed, by income, on the grid of Ipea’s Access to Opportunities Project; and, in Porto Alegre, what a fare budget leaves of that access.

Example: before and after in Porto Alegre

What-if questions answered without rebuilding the network: a new cycle path, congestion and a closed avenue, one more health facility, and a change in the fare rules, each with its map and its timing.

Example: jobs by public transport in Helsinki

A city outside Brazil, from open data: the streets of the Helsinki capital region from OpenStreetMap, HSL’s timetables, and HSY’s 250 m grids of residents and jobs; access to jobs at the morning peak, isochrones from the Central Station, and the options for one trip.
